originAxis.rationale: Where content came from, kept separate from how strongly it is supported. The existing ProvenanceLevel enum mixes both — user_direct is an origin, cross_source_confirmed is a corroboration state — which means a record cannot currently say 'this is firsthand' without also implying something about its evidential weight.

values.meaning: The account holder's own direct experience, words, capture or entry.
Behavioural history held by an external service the account holder used: playback, watch, purchase, check-in. Evidence that something happened, not a statement of what it meant.
Something another person said, about the account holder or about an event. It is that person's account, never automatically the account holder's fact.
Content extracted from a file or export the account holder supplied. The document is theirs to import; its contents are not therefore their own statement.
Produced by a deterministic, reproducible transformation of an identified source — a fingerprint, a normalised timestamp, an extracted field. Recomputable, and therefore auditable.
A model's condensation of one or more records. One model's view at one time under one prompt, never the memory itself.
A model's guess across records about something no record states. The most dangerous class: it reads like a fact and has no author.

existingVocabularyMapping.note: Approximate only. metadata_confirmed currently covers calendar and photo metadata; streaming and purchase history has no existing value.
No existing ProvenanceLevel expresses it, even though the entire shipped import pipeline produces exactly this.
No existing value. The genericcsv fingerprint is already derived content with no way to say so.

gaps.description: ProvenanceLevel conflates origin with corroboration: user_repeated and cross_source_confirmed describe how often something was seen, not where it came from.
gaps.risk: A record cannot state its origin without also asserting evidential weight, so the two can never be reasoned about independently.

gaps.description: TrustScore.evidenceCount counts evidence without requiring the pieces to be independent in origin.
gaps.risk: Duplicate amplification is built into the current contract: re-importing one export, or a repost of one original, raises confidence exactly as independent corroboration would.

gaps.description: Trust rises on 'repeated appearance' with no requirement that repetitions have distinct origins.
gaps.risk: The same failure as GAP-MEM-002 on the temporal axis: one belief written down many times becomes indistinguishable from a belief confirmed many ways.

gaps.description: No origin value exists for content produced by the shipped import pipeline or by deterministic transformation.
gaps.risk: Everything the product currently ingests is unclassifiable under the vocabulary that is supposed to classify it.

gaps.description: memory_item stores exactly one canonical_record per row with no assertion kind. The update_safe_fields policy that overwrote it in place is now closed fail-closed, but no append-only supersession exists to replace it, so a correction cannot yet be recorded at all.
gaps.risk: The destructive overwrite is prevented. The remaining gap is the absence of a non-destructive correction path, which is future work gated behind the Memory domain.

assertionAxis.rationale: What kind of claim an item makes. A 2022 entry, a 2026 reflection on 2022, and a model's summary of both are three different claims about one period, and flattening them into one field is how a life gets overwritten by its latest interpretation.

values.meaning: What was captured at the time, by the account holder or from a source. Append-only.
The account holder's own later view of an earlier record. It is a record in its own right, dated to when it was made.
A statement that an earlier item was factually wrong. It supersedes; it does not rewrite. The earlier item stays readable as what was believed then.
A model's summary, index or hypothesis. Never supersedes anything a person wrote, and never becomes a record.

invariants.statement: Content whose origin is ai_summary, ai_inferred or derived may never be stored as, promoted to, or presented as a record authored by the account holder.
invariants.preventedFailure: Interpretation Promotion and AI Output Laundering: a model's guess acquires the standing of something the person actually said.

testable.description: Enforceable once assertion kind is stored. Until then it constrains design review only, which is exactly why it is written down before the schema exists.

invariants.statement: Every stored item, of every origin, resolves to at least one source reference that identifies where it came from, and no operation may remove that reference while keeping the content.
invariants.preventedFailure: Provenance Stripping: content outliving the record of its own origin, after which nothing can tell whether a person wrote it.

testable.description: Partially holds today: memory_item.source_preview_id is NOT NULL and constrained. It is weakened by the update path recorded in GAP-MEM-005, which repoints it to a different preview.

invariants.statement: A later item never destructively updates an earlier one. Corrections and reinterpretations are new items linked to what they supersede.
invariants.preventedFailure: Silent Rewrite: the 2026 view of 2022 replacing the 2022 record, leaving no trace that the person ever thought differently.

testable.description: The destructive path is closed: update_safe_fields is refused fail-closed at the service and repository layers, and the in-place UPDATE is removed. Enforcing the positive rule — corrections stored as append-only supersession — still requires the unbuilt domain.

invariants.closedBy: services/import-api/internal/apply/service.go validateRequest and internal/pgrepo/apply.go ApplyMaterializedPreview both return ErrDuplicatePolicyUnsupported; the UPDATE memory_os.memory_item that overwrote content and provenance is deleted. Append-only supersession remains future work.

invariants.statement: Mutually contradictory interpretations of the same period may both persist. The system does not resolve them, rank them, or choose a winner.
invariants.preventedFailure: A life being flattened into a single consistent story it never had.

testable.description: Enforceable once interpretations are storable. The design constraint is that no uniqueness constraint may forbid two contradictory interpretations of one subject.

invariants.statement: Copies sharing one origin count as one piece of evidence. Re-imports, reposts, quotes, cross-device duplicates and repeated self-entry of one belief are not independent corroboration.
invariants.preventedFailure: Duplicate Amplification: frequency being mistaken for truth, which the current TrustScore contract actively enables.

testable.description: Cannot be tested until evidence counting exists. Recorded now because the existing contract already gets it wrong (GAP-MEM-002, GAP-MEM-003).

invariants.statement: Presenting several records as one event never merges their stored form. Each retains its own artifact, canonical record, retrieval path, timestamps and hashes.
invariants.preventedFailure: Context Collapse: display-level grouping quietly becoming storage-level identity, after which the evidence for the grouping cannot be re-examined.

testable.description: Constrains the future event-grouping design: grouping is a view over artifacts, never a replacement for them.

invariants.statement: Storing a memory is not consent to search it, analyse it, resurface it, or show it in the Town. These are separate permissions with separate defaults.
invariants.preventedFailure: Unauthorized Resurfacing: something deliberately set aside being pushed back into view by a feature that only checked whether it existed.

testable.description: Explicitly must not be represented as a single boolean. The set of permissions is not yet fixed, and fixing it prematurely in a schema is what this checkpoint avoids.

invariants.statement: No field, score or ranking expresses the worth, happiness, health, productivity or importance of a person or of their life. Mechanical judgements are confined to concrete inputs and security boundaries.
invariants.preventedFailure: The product becoming an instrument that grades a life.

testable.description: A schema-level check can assert that no column matching importance/score/rank/valence naming appears in memory tables. Holds today: memory_item has no such column.

invariants.statement: A collection of memories is not the person. The system does not present a simulation of the account holder, a deceased person, a family member or a partner as that person, and statements about a person are attributed to the record that carries them.
invariants.preventedFailure: Persona Reconstruction: a high-fidelity imitation being offered, or received, as the person themselves.

testable.description: Constrains any future generation surface: output about a person cites the record it came from and is phrased as what the record says, never as what the person would say.

invariants.statement: Every derivative — index, embedding, summary, hypothesis, relation, presentation preference — is reachable from the source it came from, and is erased with the account that owns it.
invariants.preventedFailure: Deletion that removes the records while leaving the model's conclusions about them.

testable.description: The deletion sweep in migration 006 currently erases nine tables. Any table added by the Memory domain must be added to sweep_deleted_account() in the same change, and the existing deletion test extended to prove it.

invariants.statement: A small, unremarkable record is a first-class memory. Nothing may drop, downrank or exclude a record on the grounds that it is minor.
invariants.preventedFailure: A memory system that only remembers what looked significant, which is the opposite of what it is for.

testable.description: Storage cost, retrieval performance and legal erasure remain real constraints and are handled as capacity decisions, never as judgements about a record's worth.

invariants.statement: A relation, grouping or attribution may only link items owned by the same account, and may never bind a record to a person on inference alone.
invariants.preventedFailure: Identity Misbinding: another person's record attaching to this account holder, or an inferred identity hardening into a stored fact.

testable.description: Enforceable exactly as the existing tenant policies are: any relation table carries owner and epoch and is covered by the same FORCE RLS predicate, so a cross-tenant link cannot be written at all.
